title: For Top Performers, Practicing Fundamentals Never Gets Old
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This post argues that elite performers stay elite because they never stop drilling the basics of their craft. It builds the case through a run of examples: choreographer Twyla Tharp, Kobe Bryant, chef Thomas Keller, and trumpeter Wynton Marsalis. Each is shown returning daily to elementary skills such as balance work, ball handling, knife skills, or long tones. The author distills the pattern into a single lesson, that excellence is the product of consistently applying fundamentals. The closing move turns the lens on the reader, asking which drills they would commit to regardless of how successful they become. The final line reframes the idea: top performers do not go back to basics because they never left them.
points: Sustained excellence across very different fields traces back to daily practice of elementary skills, not to advanced technique alone.
Fundamentals are presented as the foundation that supports advanced skills at every level of achievement, so success does not exempt anyone from them.
The author's practical prompt is to name, in advance, the basic drills you will keep doing no matter how accomplished you become.
Using Tharp, Bryant, Keller and Marsalis shows the pattern is domain-independent, which strengthens the claim for leaders' own habits.
quotes: She has practiced the same basic positions and performed the same balance exercises since she was a child. These “basics” paved the foundation for her creative success.
The late NBA player Kobe Bryant was no exception. He never took the fundamentals for granted, practicing basic ball handling, footwork, and shooting drills to start every day.

Thomas Keller is the only American-born chef to ever hold 3-star Michelin ratings for multiple restaurants. Keller’s obsession over the fundamentals, like knife skills, sautéing, and plating, produces the consistency he believes produces the excellence he strives for every day.

Marsalis always returns to the basics. Like so many other top performers, he believes the fundamentals create the foundation for more advanced skills regardless of the musician’s level of achievement.

The lesson is straightforward: Excellence in performance is the consequence of consistently practicing and applying the fundamentals. The question every performer must ask themselves is: What are the fundamental drills and exercises I should commit to no matter how successful I become?
